notes: No breadboard is used; three jumper wires connect the Arduino directly to the servo's 3-pin connector.

The circuit image shows the servo's signal wire as yellow/orange and power as red/orange-brown. The text says red = power, black = ground, white = signal. Wire colours here follow the text convention for power and ground, and the image for signal (yellow).
Signal goes to digital pin 9, as in the image and in the Sweep code (myservo.attach(9)).
Ground goes to a GND pin on the POWER header next to 5V. The catalogue has GND.1, GND.2 and GND.3, and the image doesn't say which one. GND.1 is assumed.
Wire ends at the servo are modelled as push-on joins to the servo's PWM, V+ and GND ports. Real servos have a female 3-pin connector that takes male header or jumper ends.
The first image only shows the servo's internals (DC motor, gearbox, potentiometer, control circuit). These are inside the servo part and are not separate nodes.
The Claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization (via the claude.ai connector settings). They were unavailable in this session and weren't needed for this graph.
